data.cheatsheetTitle: Explicit AC constructions for divisibility subfamilies of square presentations
data.artifactTitle: Explicit AC constructions for divisibility subfamilies of square presentations
data.artifactContent:
This is a partial result toward ordinary Andrews–Curtis, at fixed rank two.
For the ordered relator tuple

\[
G(p,s)=(u^2y^{-(2s+1)},\;uy^pu y^{-s}u^{-1}y^{-p}),
\]

we give an explicit finite AC construction for natural p,s whenever p divides
s or s+1. This includes G(2,s) for every nonnegative s. The argument passes
through a root-conjugacy pair and constructs all normal-closure substitutions
as finite ordered products of conjugates, restoring the donor relator each
time. Coordinate transports include explicit ordinary AC corrections of the
image basis. The quantified statement and its parameter consequences are
proved in Lean against the shared SAIR AC definition.

The accompanying research note explains the proof and affine entry; the
repository supplies the complete schedule, formal source and reproducible
certificate exports. Lean proves the quantified statement. Python is a
separate implementation whose emitted paths are independently replayed;
no extraction or universal equality of the two factor-list implementations
is claimed. The
50-case validation matrix passes official replay without resource limits;
48 cases meet the frozen golden budgets. Finite replay supports the exporter
and is separate from the quantified proof. No new finite challenge solves
or shortest paths are claimed.

The entire square family remains open here. For the next family G(3,3m+1),
the package proves an exact equivalence to a companion-restoration condition
at d=2,4,8,...; restoration itself remains open, including d=2. This does not
resolve AC, Stable AC, or AK(3).

The closest prior results are Ali Shehper and coauthors,
[*What makes math problems hard for reinforcement learning: a case study*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.15332v2),
whose infinite-family theorems and substitution method informed the earlier
p=1 analysis. Conjugacy/substitution techniques are credited to Pavel
Panteleev and Alexander Ushakov,
[*Conjugacy search problem and the Andrews–Curtis conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.00325).
Marc Lackenby's [thickenable-presentation theorem](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06122v1)
is a related geometric sufficient condition; its overlap with this full
arithmetic family has not been determined. Prior AC formalization by Caroline
Zhang and coauthors is acknowledged in
[*AI-Driven Mathematical Discovery for the Andrews–Curtis Conjecture*](https://openreview.net/forum?id=lt3Lpa4d2d).
The official definition and verifier are reused from
[SAIR](https://github.com/SAIRcompetition/Andrews-Curtis/tree/99a65377c5c4f412cd9af7b8d31c41464a855736),
and existing finite solved materials are credited to Lucas Fagan and coauthors'
[*Two-Hump Problem*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.21611v1) and ACSolverX work.

Our contribution is the explicit arithmetic construction and its proof
package; priority for the underlying triviality classes has not been
established. Research and preparation used Codex and Fable assistance, as
described in the paper's provenance statement.
